task_2.title: Fix crash when --cache-show and --help are passed together
task_2.description: When both --cache-show and --help CLI flags are provided simultaneously, pytest crashes with an INTERNALERROR (AttributeError) because the --cache-show path triggers a session that accesses an attribute on the Config object that has not yet been initialized when --help short-circuits normal argument parsing. The fix ensures the Config object always has the args attribute initialized from construction, and prevents the --cache-show session from running when --help is also requested, allowing the help text to display normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest with both --cache-show and --help flags does not crash with an INTERNALERROR. Previously, this combination triggered an AttributeError on the Config object because --help prevents full argument parsing, yet --cache-show unconditionally started a session that assumed parsing was complete. The fix must guarantee that --help takes precedence when combined with --cache-show, displaying the help text without errors.

expectation.grounded: The Config class must initialize the 'args' attribute (as an empty list) and 'args_source' attribute during __init__, before parse() is called, so that any code path accessing Config.args before parsing completes does not raise AttributeError. The parse() method's guard assertion must check that args is still in its initial empty state rather than checking for attribute absence. The pytest_cmdline_main hook in the cacheprovider module must check config.option.help and skip the cache-show session when --help is active, allowing the standard help flow to proceed.
expectation.conceptual: When --cache-show and --help are both provided, pytest should display the help text and exit cleanly without triggering an internal error. The Config object should always have its args attribute available regardless of how far argument parsing has progressed, so that hooks accessing it during early session stages do not crash.

constraints.grounded: The Config.args attribute must be present and set to an empty list immediately after Config construction, before any call to parse(). The parse() method must still enforce that it is only called once per Config object by verifying args is in its initial empty-list state. The --cache-show functionality must continue to work correctly when --help is not present. No new public API surface should be introduced.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the behavior of --cache-show when used alone or with other non-conflicting flags. The single-parse invariant for the Config object must be preserved. Help text output must remain unchanged. No regression in normal cache-show display or help display functionality.

behavior: Config.args is initialized as an empty list during Config.__init__, ensuring the attribute exists at all times after construction.
Config.args_source is initialized to Config.ArgsSource.ARGS during Config.__init__.
The parse() method assertion changes from checking attribute absence (hasattr) to checking that args is still an empty list, preserving the single-parse invariant.
When both --cache-show and --help options are active, the cache-show session is not started; instead, the standard help flow executes.
When --cache-show is used without --help, behavior is unchanged and cache contents are displayed normally.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest with both --cache-show and --help, it should display the help text and exit with code 0, without any INTERNALERROR.
When running pytest with --cache-show alone (no --help), it should display cached test data as before.
When running pytest with --help alone (no --cache-show), it should display the help text as before.
When accessing Config.args before parse() has been called, it should return an empty list rather than raising AttributeError.
Calling Config.parse() more than once should still raise an AssertionError indicating args can only be parsed once.

task_5.title: Make pytest.raises() recognized as ContextManager by type checkers
task_5.description: The RaisesContext class returned by pytest.raises() did not inherit from ContextManager, causing type checkers to infer its type as 'object' when used in union expressions such as 'pytest.raises(...) if cond else nullcontext()'. By deriving RaisesContext from ContextManager, type checkers can now properly narrow the type, enabling correct static analysis of conditional context-manager patterns.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.raises() is recognized by type checkers as a ContextManager, so that expressions combining pytest.raises() with other context managers (e.g., 'pytest.raises(...) if condition else nullcontext()') can be narrowed to ContextManager rather than falling back to 'object'.

expectation.grounded: The RaisesContext class should derive from typing.ContextManager parameterized with _pytest._code.ExceptionInfo[E], so that pytest.raises() is structurally and nominally a ContextManager. Type checkers (mypy, pyright) should infer the common type of 'pytest.raises(...) if cond else nullcontext()' as ContextManager rather than 'object'.
expectation.conceptual: When a user writes a conditional expression that selects between pytest.raises() and another standard context manager like nullcontext(), type checkers should infer the result as a ContextManager, enabling proper type narrowing and eliminating false-positive type errors.

constraints.grounded: RaisesContext must continue to provide __enter__ returning ExceptionInfo[E] and __exit__ with the existing signature. The existing runtime behavior of pytest.raises() as a context manager and its match keyword argument handling must remain unchanged. No existing public API signatures should break.
constraints.conceptual: The existing runtime behavior of pytest.raises() must be fully preserved. All current usages of pytest.raises() as a context manager, including exception matching and ExceptionInfo access, must continue to work identically.

behavior: RaisesContext now formally inherits from ContextManager, making it a nominal subtype of the ContextManager protocol.
Type checkers resolve the union of pytest.raises() and nullcontext() (or other ContextManagers) as ContextManager instead of object.
isinstance checks against ContextManager (contextlib.AbstractContextManager) now return True for RaisesContext instances.
The parameterized type of the ContextManager base is ExceptionInfo[E], preserving type information for the __enter__ return value.
acceptance_criteria: When a type checker analyzes 'pytest.raises(SomeError) if cond else nullcontext()', the inferred type should be ContextManager, not object.
When using pytest.raises() in a with-statement, the bound variable should still be typed as ExceptionInfo and provide access to exception attributes such as .value and .type.

When pytest.raises() is used at runtime as a context manager, it should behave identically to the previous version: entering the context, catching the expected exception, and populating ExceptionInfo on success.
When RaisesContext is checked with isinstance against contextlib.AbstractContextManager or typing.ContextManager, it should return True.
When existing tests that use pytest.raises() with the match parameter or multiple expected exception types are run, they should pass without modification.

task_1.title: Fix ZeroDivisionError in pytest.approx() for dicts with zero values
task_1.description: When using pytest.approx() to compare dictionaries containing one or more expected values of 0.0, a ZeroDivisionError was raised during the assertion failure representation. This occurred because the relative difference calculation in the dictionary-specific approximate comparison (ApproxMapping) unconditionally divided by the expected value, which fails when the expected value is zero. Lists handled this case correctly, but dictionaries did not. The fix ensures that when an expected value is 0.0, the relative difference is treated as infinity instead of attempting the division, making dictionary comparison behavior consistent with list comparison behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.approx() handles dictionaries containing zero-valued entries (0.0) without raising a ZeroDivisionError. Previously, asserting equality between two dictionaries where the expected dictionary contained 0.0 values would crash with a ZeroDivisionError during the assertion failure detail representation, while the equivalent comparison using lists worked correctly.

expectation.grounded: When pytest.approx() wraps a dictionary containing one or more 0.0 values and an equality assertion fails, the ApproxMapping class should produce a proper assertion failure message without raising ZeroDivisionError. When the expected value for a key is 0.0, the max relative difference should be set to infinity (math.inf) rather than attempting division by zero. The assertion output should display the mismatched entries with their absolute and relative differences, consistent with how ApproxSequenceLikeBase handles the same scenario for lists.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest.approx() is used with a dictionary that contains zero as an expected value and the assertion fails, a clear and informative assertion failure message should be displayed instead of an internal ZeroDivisionError. The behavior should be consistent regardless of whether the approximate comparison is performed on a dictionary or a list.

constraints.grounded: The fix must only affect the relative difference calculation within ApproxMapping when the expected value is exactly 0.0. Non-zero expected values must continue to compute relative differences via division as before. The absolute difference calculation must remain unchanged. The tolerance computation must not be affected. No other ApproxBase subclasses (ApproxNumpy, ApproxSequenceLikeBase, ApproxScalar) should be altered by this change.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the comparison logic or tolerance behavior for any non-zero expected values. Only the edge case of zero-valued expected entries in dictionary comparisons should be affected. Existing passing tests and assertion failure messages for non-zero values must remain unchanged.

behavior: When pytest.approx() wraps a dictionary and a key has an expected value of 0.0, the relative difference for that key is treated as infinity instead of computing a division by zero.

Assertion failure messages for dictionaries with 0.0 expected values now display properly, showing mismatched entries with absolute and relative differences, instead of a faulty __repr__ error caused by ZeroDivisionError.
Dictionary-based approximate comparisons with 0.0 values now behave consistently with list-based approximate comparisons that contain 0.0 values.
For non-zero expected values in dictionaries, the relative difference calculation remains unchanged (division by expected value).
acceptance_criteria: When a dictionary with an expected value of 0.0 is passed to pytest.approx() and the assertion fails, it should produce a readable assertion error message without any ZeroDivisionError.
When comparing {'key': 42.0} == pytest.approx({'key': 0.0}), the assertion should fail with a proper mismatch report showing absolute and relative differences, not a ZeroDivisionError.
When comparing [42.0] == pytest.approx([0.0]) and {'key': 42.0} == pytest.approx({'key': 0.0}), both should produce equivalently structured and informative failure messages.
When a dictionary has multiple keys and only some have 0.0 as expected values, the failure message should correctly report differences for all mismatched keys without error.
When all expected values in the dictionary are non-zero, the assertion failure output and comparison behavior must remain identical to the previous version.

task_3.title: Fix fixture named teardown being incorrectly called during nose teardown stage
task_3.description: When a pytest fixture method was named 'teardown', 'teardown_method', or 'teardown_class', the nose-compatibility teardown stage would pick it up via raw attribute lookup and attempt to call it directly. This resulted in a spurious error stating that fixtures are not meant to be called directly, even though the user never explicitly called the fixture. The fix ensures that teardown-related lookups in the Class collector use the same fixture-aware resolution already applied to setup-related lookups, so fixture-decorated methods are excluded from nose-style teardown handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that defining a pytest fixture with the name 'teardown', 'teardown_method', or 'teardown_class' on a test class does not cause it to be erroneously invoked by the nose-compatibility teardown stage. Previously, such fixtures triggered a 'Fixture called directly' error even when no user code explicitly called the fixture. This must work regardless of the fixture's scope or autouse setting.

expectation.grounded: The Class collector's teardown resolution for 'teardown_class', 'teardown_method', and the nose-fallback 'teardown' name must use the _get_first_non_fixture_func helper (the same fixture-aware lookup already used for setup_class and setup_method). When a method matching one of these names is registered as a fixture, the lookup must return None so the nose teardown stage does not attempt to call it. Non-fixture methods with these names must still be discovered and invoked normally as nose-style teardown hooks.
expectation.conceptual: When a test class defines a fixture whose name coincides with a nose-style teardown hook name, pytest must recognize it as a fixture and skip it during nose teardown resolution. The fixture should function normally through pytest's fixture mechanism, and no 'Fixture called directly' error should be raised. Plain (non-fixture) methods with these names should continue to be invoked as nose teardown hooks.

constraints.grounded: The fix must apply consistently to all three teardown name lookups in the Class collector: 'teardown_class', 'teardown_method', and the nose-fallback 'teardown'. The existing behavior for setup_class and setup_method fixture-aware resolution must not regress. Non-fixture teardown methods must still be discovered and called. The nose deprecation warning emission logic must remain intact and functional.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not alter the behavior of legitimate nose-style teardown methods that are not fixtures. Setup-side fixture-aware resolution must remain unaffected. Nose compatibility warnings must continue to be emitted where appropriate.

behavior: A fixture named 'teardown' on a test class is no longer picked up by the nose teardown stage and no longer triggers a 'Fixture called directly' error.
A fixture named 'teardown_method' on a test class is no longer picked up by the nose teardown method stage.
A fixture named 'teardown_class' on a test class is no longer picked up by the nose teardown class stage.
Non-fixture methods named 'teardown', 'teardown_method', or 'teardown_class' continue to be discovered and invoked as nose-style teardown hooks.
Fixtures named 'teardown' with autouse=True and function scope work correctly through the standard fixture mechanism without interference from nose teardown handling.
acceptance_criteria: When a test class defines an autouse fixture named 'teardown' with function scope and yields, running the test suite should produce no errors and the fixture's teardown logic should execute normally via the fixture mechanism.
When a test class defines a fixture named 'teardown_method', it should not be called directly by the nose compatibility layer, and no 'Fixture called directly' error should be raised.
When a test class defines a fixture named 'teardown_class', it should not be called directly by the nose compatibility layer, and no 'Fixture called directly' error should be raised.
When a test class defines a plain (non-fixture) method named 'teardown', it should still be invoked as a nose-style teardown hook with the appropriate deprecation warning.
When a test class has no setup or teardown methods (fixture or otherwise), the collector should skip nose-style hook registration entirely, preserving existing short-circuit behavior.

task_4.title: Fix crash when --fixtures and --help are passed together
task_4.description: When both --fixtures and --help CLI flags are passed simultaneously to pytest, the process crashes with an INTERNALERROR (AttributeError) because certain Config attributes (args_source and args) are only initialized during Config.parse(), which is never fully executed when --help triggers an early exit. The fix ensures these attributes are initialized with safe defaults at Config construction time, so they are always available regardless of whether parse() has completed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest with both --fixtures and --help flags simultaneously does not crash with an INTERNALERROR. Previously, this combination caused an AttributeError because the Config object's args_source attribute was accessed during session startup hooks before Config.parse() had a chance to initialize it. The Config object must have valid default state for args_source and args immediately after construction, so that hooks executing before or without a full parse cycle do not encounter missing attributes.

expectation.grounded: The Config class must initialize the args_source attribute (defaulting to Config.ArgsSource.ARGS) and the args attribute (defaulting to an empty list) during __init__, before parse() is called. The double-parse guard in Config.parse() must be updated to check whether args is still at its default empty-list value instead of relying on attribute existence via hasattr. When --help is passed (potentially with other flags like --fixtures), the pytest_report_header hook and any other hook accessing config.args_source must not raise an AttributeError.
expectation.conceptual: The Config object must always have a valid, well-defined state for its argument-tracking attributes from the moment it is created. Any combination of CLI flags, including --help with other informational flags, must be handled gracefully without internal errors. The mechanism that prevents double-parsing must remain functional under the new initialization strategy.

constraints.grounded: The parse-once assertion in Config.parse() must still prevent parse() from being called more than once on the same Config object. The default value of args_source (Config.ArgsSource.ARGS) must not interfere with downstream logic that inspects args_source after a successful parse. Existing behavior for all other CLI flag combinations must remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the observable behavior of pytest for any command-line invocation other than the crashing combination. The safeguard against multiple parse invocations must remain intact. Default attribute values must be neutral and not misrepresent the configuration state before parsing has occurred.

behavior: Config.__init__ now sets args_source to Config.ArgsSource.ARGS and args to an empty list as defaults, ensuring both attributes exist immediately after construction.
Config.parse() no longer checks for attribute existence (hasattr) to enforce the single-parse invariant; it instead checks whether args is still the default empty list.
When --help triggers an early exit before parse() completes, hooks like pytest_report_header that access config.args_source no longer raise AttributeError.
Running 'pytest --fixtures --help' no longer produces an INTERNALERROR traceback; it exits cleanly as --help normally would.
acceptance_criteria: When running 'pytest --fixtures --help', pytest should exit without any INTERNALERROR or AttributeError and should display help output normally.
When running 'pytest --help' alone, behavior should remain unchanged (clean help output and exit).
When running 'pytest --fixtures' alone, behavior should remain unchanged (fixtures are listed as expected).
Calling Config.parse() more than once on the same Config object should still raise an AssertionError.
After Config is constructed but before parse() is called, accessing config.args_source should return Config.ArgsSource.ARGS without raising an error.
After Config is constructed but before parse() is called, accessing config.args should return an empty list without raising an error.
All existing pytest CLI flag combinations that previously worked should continue to work without behavioral changes.

task_6.title: Document CI and BUILD_NUMBER environment variables in reference docs
task_6.description: The CI and BUILD_NUMBER environment variables were already recognized and used internally by pytest (e.g., to influence assertion introspection verbosity) but were not listed in the official Environment Variables reference section of the documentation. This change adds both variables to the docs so users can discover and understand their effect on pytest behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the CI and BUILD_NUMBER environment variables are documented in the pytest Environment Variables reference section, so that users can discover that pytest recognizes these variables and understand how they influence pytest behavior.

expectation.grounded: The Environment Variables reference section of the pytest documentation must list both the CI and BUILD_NUMBER environment variables, describing their recognized values and the observable effect they have on pytest behavior (e.g., assertion output verbosity). These variables are already consumed by pytest internally; no runtime behavior changes are introduced.
expectation.conceptual: Users consulting the pytest documentation should be able to find CI and BUILD_NUMBER in the Environment Variables reference and understand what effect setting these variables has on test execution output.

constraints.grounded: No runtime behavior of pytest must change. The CI and BUILD_NUMBER variables must continue to be recognized exactly as before. Only documentation content is affected. No public API signatures, default values, or assertion introspection logic may be altered.
constraints.conceptual: This is a documentation-only change. Existing pytest behavior when these environment variables are set or unset must remain identical.

behavior: The Environment Variables reference section now includes an entry for the CI environment variable describing its effect on pytest.
The Environment Variables reference section now includes an entry for the BUILD_NUMBER environment variable describing its effect on pytest.
No runtime behavior is modified; pytest continues to recognize CI and BUILD_NUMBER exactly as it did before this change.
acceptance_criteria: When a user views the Environment Variables reference section in the pytest documentation, they should see an entry for the CI environment variable.
When a user views the Environment Variables reference section in the pytest documentation, they should see an entry for the BUILD_NUMBER environment variable.
When CI or BUILD_NUMBER environment variables are set during test execution, pytest behavior must remain identical to the previous version (no regression).
The documentation entries for CI and BUILD_NUMBER should describe the observable effect these variables have on pytest (e.g., assertion output verbosity).

task_8.title: Clarify module-level skip documentation to explicitly describe collection prevention
task_8.description: The docstring for the `allow_module_level` parameter of `pytest.skip()` was updated to more explicitly describe the consequences of invoking a module-level skip. The previous wording only mentioned 'skipping the rest of the module', which could mislead users into thinking that tests defined before the `skip` call would still be collected. The updated wording clarifies that raising the skip exception at module level stops execution of the module and prevents the collection of all tests in that module, including those defined before the `skip` call.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documentation for `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=True)` explicitly states that a module-level skip prevents collection of all tests in the module, including tests defined before the `skip` call, and that module execution is halted entirely.

expectation.grounded: The `pytest.skip()` function's `allow_module_level` parameter documentation should state that raising the skip exception at module level stops execution of the module and prevents the collection of all tests in the module, even those defined before the `skip` call. The `Defaults to False` note for `allow_module_level` should remain present.
expectation.conceptual: The `pytest.skip()` documentation for the `allow_module_level` parameter should clearly communicate the full scope of module-level skipping: both the halt of module execution and the prevention of test collection for the entire module, not just the portion after the skip call.

constraints.grounded: The `allow_module_level` parameter's default value documentation (`Defaults to False`) must be preserved. The `reason` and deprecated `msg` parameter documentation must remain unchanged. No changes to the runtime behavior of `pytest.skip()` are permitted.
constraints.conceptual: Only the documentation wording should change. The runtime behavior of module-level skipping must remain identical. Other parameter descriptions of the `skip` function must not be affected.

behavior: The `allow_module_level` parameter docstring now explicitly states that module-level skip stops execution of the module.
The `allow_module_level` parameter docstring now explicitly states that collection of all tests in the module is prevented, including those defined before the `skip` call.
The `Defaults to False` statement for `allow_module_level` is preserved but separated into its own paragraph for clarity.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the documentation for `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=...)`, they should see an explicit statement that module-level skip prevents execution of the rest of the module.

When a user reads the documentation for `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=...)`, they should see an explicit statement that all tests in the module are prevented from being collected, including those defined before the `skip` call.
The documentation for `allow_module_level` should still indicate that the parameter defaults to False.
No runtime behavior of `pytest.skip()` is altered by this change.

task_7.title: Fix Hatch entry-points documentation example for plugin registration
task_7.description: The documentation example for registering pytest plugins via pyproject.toml using the Hatchling build backend showed an incorrect entry-points declaration syntax and included unnecessary setuptools configuration lines. The example used the generic [project.entry_points] table with array syntax, which is not the correct Hatch-specific format. The fix updates the example to use the proper [project.entry-points.pytest11] table with key-value mapping syntax as specified by Hatch's metadata configuration, and removes the extraneous [tool.setuptools] section that is irrelevant to a Hatch-based project.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documentation example for making a pytest plugin installable using pyproject.toml with the Hatchling build backend shows the correct entry-points declaration syntax. The previous example used [project.entry_points] with an array-style value, which does not conform to Hatch's metadata specification. Additionally, ensure that build-backend-specific configuration sections (e.g., [tool.setuptools]) that do not apply to Hatch-based projects are removed from the example.

expectation.grounded: The 'Writing plugins' documentation section on making plugins installable should declare the pytest11 entry-point under the [project.entry-points.pytest11] TOML table using key-value mapping syntax (e.g., plugin_name = "module.path"), consistent with Hatch's plugin metadata configuration. The [tool.setuptools] packages declaration should not appear in the Hatch-based example pyproject.toml.
expectation.conceptual: The documentation example for plugin registration via pyproject.toml should use the correct entry-point declaration format for the build backend shown in the example. Any configuration sections belonging to a different build backend should be removed so the example is self-consistent and copy-paste ready for users.

constraints.grounded: The corrected example must remain valid TOML and must correctly register a pytest11 entry-point when used with Hatchling. The example must not include [tool.setuptools] or any other setuptools-specific configuration when Hatchling is the declared build backend.
constraints.conceptual: The documentation example must be internally consistent with respect to the chosen build backend and must not mix configuration from different build systems. The example should be directly usable by a plugin author without modification beyond substituting their own project names.

behavior: The entry-points declaration in the Hatch-based pyproject.toml example changes from [project.entry_points] with array syntax to [project.entry-points.pytest11] with key-value mapping syntax.
The unnecessary [tool.setuptools] packages configuration is removed from the Hatch-based example.
No runtime behavior of pytest itself changes; this is purely a documentation correction.
acceptance_criteria: When a user views the 'Writing plugins' documentation section on making plugins installable, the pyproject.toml example for Hatch uses [project.entry-points.pytest11] as the TOML table header.
When a user views the example, the pytest11 entry-point is declared as a key-value pair (plugin_name = "module.path") rather than an array element.
When a user views the example, there is no [tool.setuptools] section present in the Hatch-based pyproject.toml.
When a user copies the corrected example pyproject.toml and builds a plugin package with Hatchling, the pytest11 entry-point should be correctly registered and discoverable by pytest.
